text:
Connor McMichael's first season in St. Louis started hot and has gone cold. The Hockey News lumped him in with Mason McTavish as Blues newcomers who have faded, and the last ten games back it up: no goals, three assists, and his ice time slipping under 13 minutes on Saturday.

There's bad luck in it. With him on the ice, St. Louis has scored 7.2 fewer goals than its chances deserve, which has cost him points, and the team's chance share with him (49%) is close to even. He's not getting buried; he's just not getting rewarded.

The worry is the other end. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season in Washington, with opponents creating more with him on the ice (bottom 5% of forwards). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says his offense lives in transition: 60% of his shots come off the rush. On a team that doesn't break out cleanly, that's a hard way to score. Our projection has him around 44 points.
